title: Out-parameters
description:
Return several results through pointers.

```
divide(17, 5): quotient 3, remainder 2
divide(1, 0): refused
parse("42"): 42
parse("4x2"): refused
```
hints: `if (quotient) *quotient = a / b;` writes only when the caller gave somewhere to write (lesson 1.04).
Build the number in a local first, and copy it into `*out` only once the whole text was valid.
requirements: `bool divide(int a, int b, int* quotient, int* remainder)` returns false for 0.
`bool parseInt(const char* text, int* out)` handles an optional `-` and digits only.
Both leave the outputs alone when they fail; passing `nullptr` for an output is allowed and skips it.
stretch: Write the same with references and with `std::optional`, and compare how the calls read. (`std::optional<int>` from `<optional>` is not covered in this course yet: look it up on cppreference; it holds either a value or nothing.)
